english.title: Knowingly cause / permit use device / substance / net / weapon / decoy / vehicle to kill / take Schedule 6 wild animal
english.standardoffencewording:
On **(..SPECIFY DATE..) at **(..SPECIFY TOWNSHIP..), for the purpose of killing or taking a wild animal included in Schedule 6 to the Wildlife and Countryside Act 1981, knowingly caused or permitted the use of

(A)_[an electrical device for killing or stunning]_
(B)_[a poisonous, poisoned or stupefying substance]_
(C)_[a net]_
(D)_[an automatic weapon, namely **(..SPECIFY AUTOMATIC WEAPON..),]_
(E)_[a semi-automatic weapon, namely **(..SPECIFY SEMI-AUTOMATIC WEAPON..),]_
(F)_[a device for illuminating a target]_
(G)_[a sighting device for night shooting]_
(H)_[a form of artificial light]_
(I)_[a mirror or other dazzling device]_
(J)_[any gas or smoke not falling within 11(2)(d)(ii) of the Wildlife and Countryside Act 1981]_
(K)_[any sound recording used as a decoy]_
(L)_[a mechanically propelled vehicle, namely **(..SPECIFY VEHICLE..), in immediate pursuit of such an animal]_
(M)_[**(..SPECIFY WHERE MORE THAN ONE OF THE ABOVE OPTIONS USED IN SAME INCIDENT..)]_
english.legislation: Contrary to sections 11(2)(d), 11(2)(f) and 21(1) of the Wildlife and Countryside Act 1981.

investigatoraction.description: Guilty Plea by letter procedure may be offered for this offence

DNA Samples: If crime scene stain present - take evidential sample If no crime scene stain and DNA not confirmed on PNC - take Criminal Justice sample. If DNA confirmed on PNC - CJ sample not required
Confirm proposed charge is appropriately authorised (Police or CPS)
Ensure compliance with investigator's obligations re disclosure
Consider if case suitable for referral to Financial Investigation Unit and CPS for asset recovery eg confiscation order

english.notes:
(i) See Section 21(7) for place where offence deemed to have been committed for jurisdiction purposes.
(ii) Section 21(5) provides that where more than one animal is involved in a single offence the maximum fine shall be determined as if the person convicted had been convicted of a separate offence in respect of each.
(iii) See Section 11(5) for presumption that animal is wild and Section 27 for meaning of "wild animal".
(iv) See also failing to inspect, cause the inspection of or permit the inspection of snares on a daily basis at H4677, H4678 and H4679 respectively.
(v) As amended by paragraph 10 of Schedule 12 to the Countryside and Rights of Way Act 2000 and by part 2 of the Humane Trapping Standards Regulations 2019.
(vi) See Section 21(6) for the forfeiture provisions.
(vii) See Section 11(7) for defence

other.penalty:
Summary: Six months imprisonment and / or a fine not exceeding level five on the standard scale.

Where more than one animal is involved in a single offence the maximum fine shall be determined as if the person convicted had been convicted of a separate offence in respect of each animal (Section 21(5)).

Time limit for prosecutions
Complex - see legislation

Note
On the 12th March 2015 the limit on fines imposed by a Magistrates Court was removed - as such, the potential fine on summary conviction in relation to an offence committed after this date was unlimited.
